# sidharthify

> Personal site of sidharth (also goes by siddhi; online handle "sidharthify"), a systems and android developer who works across the stack: the AOSP framework and linux kernels, native android and iOS apps, and FastAPI backends. sidharth is the lead developer and maintainer of breatheOSS.

Facts to get right:

- "sidharthify" is a handle. The person is sidharth. The site is sidharthify.tech.
- sidharth leads breatheOSS (https://breatheoss.app), an open-source, community-driven air quality network for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. It runs its own AirGradient sensors in Jammu, Srinagar and Rajouri, backed by satellite models. The FastAPI backend computes both the Indian (CPCB) and US EPA AQI. There are android (kotlin, compose), iOS (swift, swiftui) and web clients, a discord bot, an open data repository and a governance charter. Project info: https://about.breatheoss.app, code: https://github.com/breathe-OSS
- sidharth maintains devices for the custom ROMs YAAP (Yet Another AOSP Project) and cipherOS. sidharth also brought up the Xiaomi Pad 8 for AOSP from scratch.
- sidharth runs NixOS as a daily driver, fully declarative, with a small homelab.
- sidharthify.tech is hand-written in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no frameworks.

## Pages

- [Home](https://sidharthify.tech/): overview, projects and skills
- [About](https://sidharthify.tech/about/): background, interests and beliefs
- [Blog](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/): index of all posts

## Projects

- breatheOSS: lead dev & maintainer. Open-source air quality network for J&K and Ladakh. https://breatheoss.app
- breatheForecaster: seven day PM2.5 / PM10 / AQI forecaster for the breatheOSS network, written in pure standard-library python. Forecasts are published nightly before the days happen and graded in public afterwards.
- YAAP (yet another aosp project): maintainer / contributor. https://github.com/yaap
- cipherOS: maintainer. https://cipheros.org.in
- Device trees and ports: Nothing Phone 2a/2a+, realme 8i / narzo 50 4g, realme 9 5g SE, Pixel 7 / 7 Pro. Roles across these: maintainer, co-lead, contributor, tester.
- LineageOS contributions: rewriting legacy HIDL hardware abstraction layers to AIDL, building kernels.
- Xiaomi Pad 8 bring-up: AOSP device bring-up done from scratch (device tree, vendor and kernel), with syd as its kernel.
- syd (kernel): a custom android kernel for the Pixel 7 and the Xiaomi Pad 8. The Pixel 7 kernel was ported to Linux 6.12.
- syd (NixOS tool): a separate, unrelated project that shares the name. A lightweight command-line helper tool for NixOS, packaged for nixpkgs.
- CWR engine port (ARMA Cold War Assault): ported a 20-year-old C++ game engine to android arm64 with a custom OpenGL ES 3.2 backend.
- NixOS homelab: a modded minecraft server run as a systemd service, with a discord bot that starts it on request and stops it by in-game majority vote, ipv6 ddns, a playit tunnel and daily backups. Sunshine for game streaming.
- stillAlive-C: the Portal ending credits recreated in pure C for the terminal, with typed-out text, ascii art and audio in sync.
- ladsave: save editor in C for Yakuza: Like a Dragon on linux. Reverses the xor + crc32 save format and splices bytes in place.
- bcstm2wav: batch converts Nintendo 3DS .bcstm audio to .wav, written in C.

## Skills

- C and modern C++: engine rendering backends, kernelspace C, AOSP C++, custom math libraries
- AOSP: device trees, HALs (AIDL/HIDL), soong, Android.bp, overlays, fastboot, adb
- Graphics: OpenGL ES 3.2, GLSL vertex/fragment shaders, rewriting fixed-function pipelines
- Nix/NixOS: flakes, the distro and the nix language
- Kotlin (android), Swift (iOS), Python, Bash, HTML/CSS/JavaScript
- Linux kernel builds, including moving the Pixel kernel pipeline off Bazel

## Blog posts

- [Porting the Pixel 7 kernel to Linux 6.12](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-12-10-26/) (2026-10-12): Moving my gs201 kernel from 6.1 to 6.12, and the twelve bugs between a crash on the Google logo and a working camera.
- [Porting ARMA CWA to Android ARM64](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-28-06-26/) (2026-06-28): Getting the CWR engine (ARMA: Cold War Assault) running on modern Android hardware.
- [Exposing the Lies Behind CBSE's OnMark Portals](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-31-05-26/) (2026-05-31): Almost all OnMark websites from EduTek are fundamentally insecure, and CBSE is lying about it.
- [Creating an open-source & accurate AQI service for J&K](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-10-2-26/) (2026-02-10): A deep dive into how I built a community initiative to provide accurate air quality data for Jammu & Kashmir.
- [Breaking free from Bazel in the Pixel kernel pipeline](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-14-12-25/) (2025-12-14): Rebuilding the Pixel kernel pipeline without Bazel, and understanding GKI, DLKM, VINTF, and Android's implicit kernel contracts.
- [Writing a Nix helper script](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-18-10-25/) (2025-10-18): A lightweight Python CLI tool for managing NixOS packages declaratively, born from a random Thursday evening.
- [Fixing Google's cluttered device trees](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-25-06-25/) (2025-06-25): Cleaning up Google's messy device tree structure for Pixel phones in AOSP.
- [How AOSP Device Trees are structured](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-22-05-25/) (2025-05-22): A breakdown of how AOSP device trees are laid out: makefiles, configs, overlays, and sepolicy.
- [How I got into Android ROM development and Linux](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-18-05-25/) (2025-05-18): A personal account of diving into Android Open Source development for the first time.
- [Dealing with AIDL](https://sidharthify.tech/blogs/blog-17-05-25/) (2025-05-17): Rewriting the PowerShare HAL from HIDL to AIDL and contributing it upstream to LineageOS.
